inputs.content: Refactor objective: share duplicated enabled-row selection in report.py without changing enabled_names(rows) or enabled_total(rows). Only report.py and tests/test_report.py may change; no new production modules. Inputs are finite iterables of mappings, including one-shot generators. Include a row only when row["enabled"] is True (not merely truthy). Preserve order and duplicate names; return a list of original name objects and a numeric sum starting at integer 0. Do not mutate inputs. Missing enabled raises KeyError("enabled"); on an enabled row, the selected function requires only its own name/amount field and raises the corresponding KeyError when absent. Disabled rows need neither field. Each function consumes its input once, checks enabled exactly once per row, reads the selected field once per enabled row and never reads the other field. No full-input buffering before processing: finish a row before requesting the next. These bounded access/streaming contracts stand in for complexity, without timing benchmarks. Run python -B -m unittest discover -s tests.

import unittest
from report import enabled_names, enabled_total

class ReportTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_order_duplicates_and_strict_enabled(self):
        rows = [dict(enabled=True, name='B', amount=3),
                dict(enabled=1, name='skip', amount=100),
                dict(enabled=True, name='A', amount=-1),
                dict(enabled=True, name='B', amount=2)]
        self.assertEqual(enabled_names(iter(rows)), ['B', 'A', 'B'])
        self.assertEqual(enabled_total(iter(rows)), 4)

    def test_empty_and_missing_fields(self):
        self.assertEqual(enabled_names(iter([])), [])
        self.assertEqual(enabled_total(iter([])), 0)
        self.assertEqual(enabled_names([{'enabled': False}]), [])
        with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
            enabled_names([{'enabled': True}])
        with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
            enabled_total([{'enabled': True}])
